name: windows-firewall-on
title: Turn on firewall profiles that are off
description: Turns on the Windows Firewall profiles (Domain, Private, Public) that are off, unless Group Policy controls them, and reads the effective state (ActiveStore) back. Turning a profile on can block inbound traffic that worked only because the firewall was off (printer or scanner sharing, imaging or lab interfaces); the preview lists inbound connections in use now.
manualUndo: Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile <the profiles listed as turned on> -Enabled False
measure: foreach ($f in @(Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/SecurityCenter2 -ClassName FirewallProduct -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Add-ArhInfo 'Other firewall' $f.displayName }
Add-ArhInfo 'Inbound connections now' $(if ($ports.Count) { "$($inbound.Count) on port(s) " + ($ports -join ', ') } else { 'none' })
if ($ports.Count) { Add-ArhWarning ('Inbound connections are in use on port(s) ' + ($ports -join ', ') + '; a profile turned on may block them unless a rule allows them') }
foreach ($n in @($off | Where-Object { $gpo.ContainsKey($_) })) { Add-ArhBlocker "Group Policy keeps the $n profile off" }

if ($todo.Count) { Set-ArhPlan $true ('Turn on: ' + ($todo -join ', ')) } else { Set-ArhPlan $false $(if ($off.Count) { 'Only profiles Group Policy controls are off' } else { 'All profiles are on' }) }
